audit.whatIsWrong: Subjugate is described everywhere as a resistance drain and nothing else — "drains a percentage of your armour and MR". It also deals 20/25/30% of the target's MAXIMUM HEALTH as magic damage and heals Trundle for exactly that amount, half instantly and half over the following 4 seconds.
audit.why: This is the whole matchup. Tahm Kench builds Heartsteel and stacks health; every point of it makes Subjugate hit harder and heal Trundle more. The entry currently tells the player the opposite in whys[5] — that Heartsteel means "even a Subjugate drain does not out-pace Thick Skin's conversion" — which sends a Tahm Kench into the one ultimate in the game that scales off his own build.
audit.corrected: Subjugate (120/100/80s, 650 range, 0.25s cast, uninterruptible): 40% of current armour and MR, plus 20/25/30% of your max health as damage and the same again as healing for Trundle.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] says Trundle wants to "Land Subjugate early ... before you build the resistances that make it less meaningful". Subjugate steals 40% of the resistances you are carrying at the moment it lands.
audit.why: Buying armour and MR makes the steal bigger, not smaller. A player following this line believes his Thornmail and Spirit Visage are Subjugate insurance when they are the opposite.
audit.corrected: Trundle wants Subjugate AFTER your resistance purchases, not before — 40% of a bigger number is a bigger number.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid and whys[4] call Tahm Kench's W "Abyssal Voyage" and describe it as "a global safety valve and roam threat" and "a repositioning escape" that lets you simply leave the lane.
audit.why: Tahm Kench has no global ability. Abyssal Dive is a 1.35-second channel into a 1000-1200 range blink on a 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown — an engage, and a slow one. Advising it as an escape from a Trundle who has just walked onto his Frozen Domain gets a player killed mid-channel.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is Devour, not an escape. Abyssal Dive is a telegraphed engage you spend after the stun, and Pillar of Ice's 6 seconds of real terrain is what actually threatens your retreat.
sources: League Wiki — Tahm Kench: Abyssal Dive
League Wiki — Trundle: Pillar of Ice

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] ("Lvl 3"), mid and whys[2] all describe landing "stun into Devour" at level 3. Devour is the ultimate and arrives at 6.
audit.why: It promises a kill pattern three levels before it exists, and it makes the level-3 spike look bigger than it is. At 3 the punish is the 1.5-second stun and the auto chain that follows it.
audit.corrected: Level 3: three stacks, 1.5s Tongue Lash stun, auto chain. Level 6: the same setup now ends in Devour.
sources: League Wiki — Tahm Kench: Tongue Lash

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere. "Play around his Subjugate cooldown" is stated without a single number, and Frozen Domain — the ability that actually decides every extended trade — has no timing attached to it at all.
audit.why: Frozen Domain is 18/17/16/15/14s and lasts 8 seconds, giving +25% healing from all sources and up to +90% attack speed. Chomp is a 3.5-second attack reset, so on his zone he gets an empowered bite roughly every other auto. The rule is not 'trade when Subjugate is down' — it is 'trade when Frozen Domain has expired'.
audit.corrected: Wait for Frozen Domain's 8 seconds to run out before committing; Subjugate is 120/100/80s, so once he spends it you own a very long window.
sources: League Wiki — Trundle: Frozen Domain, Chomp

audit.why: Early anti-heal is correctly flagged as core. King's Tribute heals him for 1.8-5.94% of the max health of every unit that dies near him and Frozen Domain amplifies all healing he receives by 25%, so Grievous Wounds applied before the extended trade rather than during it is the right instruction.
sources: League Wiki — Trundle: King's Tribute, Frozen Domain

edits.before: You remain a strong frontliner because your Thick Skin grey-health healing and point-and-click Devour lockdown scale with your tank items rather than with raw damage — Trundle's Subjugate resistance drain hurts more as his passive stacks and your resistances rise, so do not aimlessly soak his R without activating Thick Skin for the immediate shield. In teamfights, peel your carries and use Devour to pull Trundle off them, reversing his drain threat; a Devoured Trundle loses all of his Frozen Domain repositioning and Pillar angles while the hold lasts. Both sides are durable enough that this lane resolves into a resource war — you win it by keeping a clean An Acquired Taste stacking pattern all game rather than attempting raw duels in his Frozen Domain.
